history.sg_progress: The Board issued the recommendation in paragraph 57 of its report for the year ended 31 December 2018 (A/74/5 (Vol. I)) on strengthening the system of capitalization of intangible assets, when it noted that software licences were directly expensed in 2018 and later capitalized in 2019. The Administration implemented stronger reviews of intangible capitalization for the project, ensuring that the project structures were functional and in place. In 2021, the Board identified an additional $24.8 million of expenditure requiring capitalization for the Umoja project from 2015 to 2021. The Administration submitted supporting documentation to the Board, proving that $0.6 million of expenditure relating to 2021 was correctly expensed, which was accepted by the Board. The Administration has agreed to provide the Board with supporting documentation confirming the valid treatment of the remaining amount of $24.2 million by the second quarter of 2023.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration review the listed records and provide more guidance to relevant departments and offices on asset capitalization to ensure that relevant project expenditure is appropriately classified and recorded in Umoja in the future.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers that the first part of the recommendation, with regard to the review of expenditure and the capitalization of the flexible workplace project, has been implemented. The Administration reiterates that strong financial controls exist in the area of capitalization. In addition, all assets are included in the key performance indicator reviews undertaken by the Global Asset Management Policy Service, which aims at ensuring that assets are correctly capitalized. The Administration has also implemented stronger reviews of intangible asset capitalization with offices. Specifically, in relation to the initial observation regarding the capitalization of flexible workspace and Umoja, when costs are incurred related to the Umoja project, the Enterprise Resource Planning Solution Division defines whether a cost is capitalizable through the use of the appropriate work breakdown structure element. All costs related to the flexible workspace were capitalized in 2021. During the 2021 audit, the Board identified expenditures requiring capitalization and the Administration submitted supporting documentation to the Board for those costs showing that they were correctly expensed. The Administration again reiterates that the Umoja project expenditures are correctly treated and will provide additional documentation as required.
history.board_assessment: Given that supporting documentation related to the expenditure has not been provided, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.administration_response: The Administration reiterates that IPSAS corporate guidance and IPSAS guidance on the capitalization of Umoja provides detailed guidance concerning the classification of capitalizable and non-capitalizable expenditure. In addition, project structures are set up to manage the collection of costs, and the division of capitalizable and non-capitalizable expenditure. In addition, in relation to the specific expenditure mentioned, the Administration has provided supporting documentation relating to the expenditure, in line with the Board’s comments. Therefore, the Administration requests an opportunity to discuss the supporting documentation provided to the Board to clarify that the recommendation was implemented as evidenced by the review carried out. (Supporting documentation has been uploaded to the Board’s repository)
history.board_assessment: Given that the Board has not been provided with sufficient supporting documentation, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.
